new_scholarship.name: Émile Boutmy Scholarship
new_scholarship.description: The Émile Boutmy Scholarship is a tuition-fee exemption created by Sciences Po to welcome high-achieving international students from outside the European Union. It is awarded to first-time applicants admitted to the Undergraduate College or to a two-year Master's programme. At Undergraduate College level it gives either a total exemption or a €9,500 tuition-fee exemption; at Master's level it gives a €18,500 exemption from tuition fees for each of the two years. It cannot be combined with other Sciences Po or partner scholarships.
new_scholarship.duration: Bachelor's: tuition-fee grant for the first year, retained during the third year abroad. Master's: €18,500 tuition-fee exemption for each of the two years of the programme.

Deadline for master programme: 18 October (1st committee, results before December 20) or 29 November (2nd committee, results before March 2).

new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: First-time applicants to Sciences Po from a non-European Union state whose household does not file taxes within the European Union, admitted to the Undergraduate College or to a two-year Master's programme. Applicants who are already enrolled at Sciences Po cannot apply.

new_scholarship.name: HEC Paris Scholarships (Merit-Based and Need-Based)
new_scholarship.description: HEC Paris runs two families of scholarships for Master's and MBA applicants: merit-based awards decided automatically once a candidate is admitted, and need-based awards requiring a separate form in the Applicant Space. All merit-based awards are tuition-fee reductions, ranging from €5,000 (AVENIR) to up to €20,000 (Women in Finance & Technology), with several awards of up to €10,000–€15,000. Need-based awards include up to 35% of tuition fees (Equal Opportunity), €15,000 per Master's year (Garzouzi) and case-by-case jury amounts (Imagine Fellowship, CMA-CGM). Four admissions rounds each carry a 12pm noon need-based deadline, starting with 26 October 2026.

Awards take the form of tuition-fee waivers of 25%, 50%, 75% or 100%, plus a limited number of fully-funded scholarships that cover 100% of fees and may add a stipend. new_scholarship.description: The A*STAR Graduate Scholarship offers full funding for a PhD at a Singapore autonomous university, with joint supervision by an A*STAR researcher and a university faculty member. programme_detail_official.description: The A*STAR Graduate Scholarship offers full funding for a PhD at a Singapore autonomous university, with joint supervision by an A*STAR researcher and a university faculty member. Successful applicants receive full tuition fees, a monthly sustenance allowance inclusive of CPF contribution where applicable, book, computer, conference and thesis allowances, and support for up to 12 months of overseas attachment, for up to 4 years. For international students the monthly allowance is $3,600 on the STEM track or $5,000 on the specialised Semiconductor, Quantum and Computing tracks. The scholarship is bond-free for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents; non-Singaporean awardees without Permanent Residency must serve 3 years in a Singapore-based company. Applications run 1 November to 1 February and 1 June to 10 August.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you hold, or are in the last semester of, a Bachelor's or Master's degree from a Singapore autonomous university, which international applicants must have
Secure an A*STAR researcher and a university faculty member willing to co-supervise before you apply, since the proposal is developed with them

Ask the A*STAR supervisor for the endorsement package: project summary, willingness to co-supervise, reasons for support, rationale for university collaboration, and confirmation that the research sits at an A*STAR Research Institute
Pick your track, since the specialised Semiconductor, Quantum and Computing tracks pay $5,000 instead of $3,600
Have your CV ready before creating the application account
Arrange at least 2 referee reports, with a current university supervisor as one of them for mid-term applicants
Apply to a partner university concurrently, because the award is conditional on confirmation of placement
Be certain you can meet the 3-year service commitment in a Singapore-based company if you are not a Permanent Resident
common_rejection_risks: Holding a degree from outside Singapore without a Singapore autonomous university place, which blocks international applicants
Not securing an A*STAR co-supervisor, or a supervisor not approved by A*STAR
Missing a cycle: the window is closed between 10 August and 1 November
Submitting without the supervisor's endorsement package
Assuming the scholarship is bond-free as a foreigner: only Citizens and PRs are, and a non-PR international must serve 3 years
Holding a Second Class (Lower) degree and expecting rejection: A*STAR states it assesses each application holistically, including research experience and achievements
Planning a change of research project later without A*STAR's written permission

submission_workflow: Identify an A*STAR research project or researcher and a university faculty member willing to co-supervise
Develop the research proposal with both supervisors, aligned to Singapore's RIE ecosystem
Obtain the A*STAR supervisor's written endorsement with the required confirmation items
Prepare your CV, then create your account in the A*STAR scholarship portal
Submit the application with at least 2 referee reports, the research area description and all academic credentials in the open cycle
Apply to a partner autonomous university for admission concurrently
Attend at least two rounds of interviews with BRC or SERC senior management and A*STAR researchers
Await notification by email; the process typically takes about 5 months
